The **2024 WTA Finals** was the [professional women's year-end championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WTA_Finals "WTA Finals") [tennis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennis "Tennis") tournament run by the [Women's Tennis Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_Tennis_Association "Women's Tennis Association") (WTA). It was the 53rd edition of the singles event and the 48th edition of the doubles competition and took place between 2 and 9 November. The tournament was contested by the eight highest-ranked singles players and doubles teams of the [2024 WTA Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_WTA_Tour "2024 WTA Tour"). It took place in [Riyadh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riyadh "Riyadh"), [Saudi Arabia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabia "Saudi Arabia"), marking its return to Asia for the first time since [2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_WTA_Finals "2019 WTA Finals"), and the fifth consecutive finals to be held in a different city ([Shenzhen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shenzhen "Shenzhen") in 2019, [Guadalajara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guadalajara "Guadalajara") in [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_WTA_Finals "2021 WTA Finals"), [Fort Worth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Worth,_Texas "Fort Worth, Texas") in [2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_WTA_Finals "2022 WTA Finals"), and [Cancún](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canc%C3%BAn "Cancún") in [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_WTA_Finals "2023 WTA Finals")). This was the first time that Saudi Arabia hosted the tournament.

## Tournament
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_WTA_Finals&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Tournament")]
### Qualifying
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_WTA_Finals&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Qualifying")]
Eight players/teams to compete in singles/doubles.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_WTA_Finals#cite_note-1) To qualify, players/teams have to play a minimum of eight WTA 1000 or WTA 500 tournaments during the season. Players/teams are qualified in the following sequence:
  1. Ranked top seven in the leaderboard;
  2. The highest-ranked current-year Grand Slam winning player/team ranked from eighth to twentieth;
  3. The second-highest-ranked current-year Grand Slam winning player/team ranked from eighth to twentieth, if one player/team ranked in the top seven withdraws;
  4. The next player who is ranked eighth or below.


In the singles, point totals are calculated by combining point totals from eighteen tournaments (excluding [ITF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITF_Women's_World_Tennis_Tour "ITF Women's World Tennis Tour") and [WTA 125](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WTA_125K_series "WTA 125K series") tournaments). Of these eighteen tournaments, a player's results from the following events are included:
  * The four [Grand Slam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Slam_\(tennis\) "Grand Slam \(tennis\)") events;
  * Six best mandatory [WTA 1000 tournaments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WTA_1000_tournaments "WTA 1000 tournaments") from the following seven events: [Indian Wells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Wells_Open "Indian Wells Open"), [Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Open_\(tennis\) "Miami Open \(tennis\)"), [Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid_Open_\(tennis\) "Madrid Open \(tennis\)"), [Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Open_\(tennis\) "Italian Open \(tennis\)"), [Toronto/Montreal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Open_\(tennis\) "Canadian Open \(tennis\)"), [Cincinnati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati_Open "Cincinnati Open") and [Beijing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_Open_\(tennis\) "China Open \(tennis\)");
  * The best mandatory WTA 1000 tournament from the following three events: [Doha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WTA_Qatar_Open "WTA Qatar Open"), [Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai_Tennis_Championships "Dubai Tennis Championships") and [Wuhan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wuhan_Open "Wuhan Open");
  * (for the players who played the main draw of least two such tournaments) the best seven results from any other mandatory WTA 1000, [WTA 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WTA_500_tournaments "WTA 500 tournaments") and [WTA 250 tournaments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WTA_250_tournaments "WTA 250 tournaments").


In the doubles, point totals are calculated by any combination of twelve tournaments throughout the year. Unlike in the singles, this combination does not need to include results from the Grand Slams or WTA 1000 tournaments.
### Format
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_WTA_Finals&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Format")]
Both the singles and doubles event features eight players/teams in a [round-robin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Round-robin_tournament "Round-robin tournament") event, split into two groups of four.
Over the first six days of competition, each player/team meets the other three players/teams in her group, with the top two in each group advancing to the semifinals. The first-placed player/team in one group meets the second-placed player/team in the other group, and vice versa. The winners of each semifinal meet in the championship match.
### Round robin tie-breaking methods
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_WTA_Finals&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Round robin tie-breaking methods")]
The final standings are made using these methods:
  1. Greatest number of match wins
  2. Greatest number of matches played
  3. Head-to-head results if only two players are tied, or if three players are tied then:

         a. If three players each have the same number of wins, a player having played less than all three matches is automatically eliminated and the player advancing to the single-elimination competition is the winner of the match-up of the two remaining tied players.     b. Highest percentage of sets won     c. Highest percentage of games won
## Prize money and points
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_WTA_Finals&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Prize money and points")]
The total prize money for the 2024 WTA Finals is US$15,250,000, an increase of 69.44% compared to the 2023 edition.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_WTA_Finals#cite_note-eventinfo-2) The tables below break down the prize money, participation fees are prorated on a per match basis.

| --- | --- | --- |  
| Singles  | Doubles[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_WTA_Finals#cite_note-doublesmoney-3)  |  
| Champion  | RR[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_WTA_Finals#cite_note-Rrobin-4) + $3,770,000  | RR[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_WTA_Finals#cite_note-Rrobin-4) + $775,000  | RR + 900  |  
| Runner-up  | RR + $1,270,000  | RR + $255,000  | RR + 400  |  
| Round robin win per match  | +$350,000  | +$70,000  | 200  |

  1. [↑](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_WTA_Finals#cite_ref-doublesmoney_3-0 "Jump up") Prize money for doubles is per team.
  2. [Jump up to: 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_WTA_Finals#cite_ref-Rrobin_4-0) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_WTA_Finals#cite_ref-Rrobin_4-1) RR means prize money or points won in the round-robin round. 


  * An undefeated champion would earn the maximum 1,500 points and $5,155,000 in singles or $1,125,000 in doubles.
  * Participation fees are prorated on a per match basis. Singles: 1 match = $225,000 2 matches = $275,000 and 3 matches = $335,000. Doubles: 1 match = $94,000 2 matches = $116,000 and 3 matches = $140,000.
  * Alternate fees are also prorated on a per-match basis. Singles: 0 matches = $140,000, 1 match = $200,000, 2 matches = $250,000. Doubles: 0 matches= $60,000, 1 match = $84,000, 2 matches= $106,000
